headline: Activity Permits and Seasonal Campground Access
reservation: While entry to Wayne National Forest is generally free, specific permits are required for motorized trail use and dispersed camping in certain management areas. Developed campgrounds are seasonally managed and may require advanced booking through the official federal portal; always verify current opening dates before arrival.

days.title: High Ridges and Pine Forests

stops.name: Wildcat Hollow Trailhead
stops.detail: Hike the 5-mile loop through dense pine plantations and Appalachian rock formations.

stops.name: Court Street
stops.detail: Experience the local culture and historic architecture of the Athens gateway community.

days.driving: Allow 90 minutes from PKB airport to Athens; local forest roads are winding.
days.note: Trail conditions in Wildcat Hollow can be muddy in early spring; wear waterproof footwear.

days.title: River Crossings and Historic Spans

stops.name: Hune Covered Bridge
stops.detail: View this 19th-century engineering landmark along the Little Muskingum River.

stops.name: Scenic River Trail
stops.detail: Trek to overlooks providing expansive views of the river valley and forested hills.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the Covered Bridge Scenic Byway; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: The Scenic Byway is narrow; use caution when encountering oncoming traffic or cyclists.

days.title: Lake Vesuvius Exploration

stops.name: Rock House Trail
stops.detail: Navigate a moderate path to a massive sandstone rock shelter used by early settlers.

stops.name: Vesuvius Dam
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk for views of the steep cliffs and calm waters of the recreation area.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the return trip to PKB airport; rural roads require a slower pace.
days.note: Lake Vesuvius is a popular weekend spot; weekdays offer more seclusion for hikers.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking at popular trailheads like Lake Vesuvius can fill during autumn weekends; arrive early. Most remote trailheads offer gravel pull-offs with limited space for larger vehicles.

intel.title: Rural Connectivity
intel.text: Expect zero cellular service in the Marietta and Ironton units; download offline maps before leaving gateway towns. A physical road atlas is recommended for navigating the maze of forest service roads.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Athens and Marietta serve as the primary fuel hubs; gas stations are non-existent within the forest interior. Ensure your tank is full before departing for the Covered Bridge Scenic Byway.

intel.title: Hunting Season Awareness
intel.text: Be aware of local hunting seasons in the fall and winter; wearing blaze orange is a standard safety practice for hikers. Spring wildflowers peak in late April, while fall colors usually crest in mid-October.

intel.title: Road Maintenance
intel.text: Some forest roads are not maintained for winter travel and may be impassable after heavy rain. Check the official Forest Service website for current alerts on bridge closures or storm damage.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at PKB, drive 90 minutes west to Athens for supplies and check-in at a local lodge.
plan.vehicle: An SUV or 4WD vehicle is recommended for forest service roads, though main byways are paved. Check rental terms for off-pavement use.
plan.goldenHour: Little Muskingum River overlooks for sunset, with seasonal leaf-drop enhancing the view.
